records.swap_audit:
==== SWAP AUDIT — why each detected face was or was not swapped ====
  faces seen                                                       936  100.0%
    of those, crop shared with the face beside it                  125   13.4%
    of those, gap-filled                                            34    3.6%
  swapped (identity lock)                                          767   81.9%
  no track entry matched                                           122   13.0%
  refused: crop shared with the face beside it                      89    9.5%
  fallback missed (over match threshold)                            48    5.1%
  veto: source used twice in frame                                  47    5.0%
  swapped (per-frame match)                                         32    3.4%
    of those, partly behind an object (masked, still swapped)      354   37.8%
    of those SWAPPED, gap-filled                                     2    0.2%
  -> 137 of 936 detected faces (14.6%) were NOT swapped.
     Frames where a face was found but left un-swapped are what reads as flicker. The largest refusal line above is the gate to loosen.
     2 of the 799 faces actually swapped (0.3%) had INTERPOLATED landmarks — nobody detected them, their box and keypoints were filled in between neighbours.
     That is a different artefact from the one above: the swap is not missing, it is registered from a guess, so on a moving head it shifts every other frame. Set ROOP_TEMPORAL_STEP=1 if this is high.
     Of those, 48 were refused for distance alone, and this is how far past the match threshold (0.75) their BEST candidate sat:
       within 1.05x the threshold (0.79):       1  (  2.1% of them)
       within 1.10x the threshold (0.83):       3  (  6.2% of them)
       within 1.20x the threshold (0.90):      13  ( 27.1% of them)
       within 1.50x the threshold (1.12):      48  (100.0% of them)
       within 2.00x the threshold (1.50):      48  (100.0% of them)
       median refusal sits at 1.25x the threshold (0.93).
     Separately, 144 frames of 744 (19.4% of frames) had NO face detected at all — that is the detector losing the face, not a gate refusing it, so it is a different problem from every refusal above.
     (no detector scores recorded — only retinaface reports them; on another engine, compare engines or raise the detector resolution.)
